raw_text: member_002 here, acting as independent reviewer for REVIEW2. No fixed candidate is published yet (patches=0). Please implement the fix for "Require a non-empty name for Blueprints" (raise ValueError when a Blueprint name is empty), publish it with fix_patch, then send me a handoff_patch with the patch_id. I will integrate it, run the public tests on that exact version, and accept or request changes. Note: in REVIEW2 I must accept your exact final fixed version before delivery, so please hand off the final candidate once it's ready.

Final candidate published: patch-1 (changed file: src/flask/blueprints.py only).

Behavior change: in `Blueprint.__init__`, immediately after `super().__init__(...)` and before the existing dot check, it now does:
    if not name:
        raise ValueError("'name' may not be empty.")
So `flask.Blueprint("", __name__)` raises ValueError, while an empty-but-non-empty-checked dotted name still raises the existing "'name' may not contain a dot '.' character." ValueError. No other callers/tests construct a Blueprint with an empty name (I grepped tests/), so nothing existing should regress.

Please integrate_patch(patch-1), run the public tests on that exact version, and org_review_patch accept or request changes. Do not edit the candidate yourself; if you want a behavior tweak, request changes and I will republish a new patch.

Important harness note: when I ran the public tests on this exact version (both focused `pytest tests/test_blueprints.py` and the full entrypoint), pytest died at startup before collecting anything, with `pytest.PytestAssertRewriteWarning: Module already imported so cannot be rewritten: pws_public_test_evidence_v141`, raised from `_pytest/config/__init__.py:736 consider_env()` -> `_import_plugin_specs(os.environ.get("PYTEST_PLUGINS"))`. So it is the harness-injected PYTEST_PLUGINS plugin, not a test-case failure from this diff; report validation_status is "failed" with counts all null and 0 collected. Expect the same in your run — please record that honestly rather than treating it as a regression of the candidate.

Review decision recorded: review-1 = request_changes on patch-1 (rework responsible: you). Not a code objection — please read the reason.

CODE: I adopted patch-1 (my tree now v2) and confirmed the diff directly. src/flask/blueprints.py adds, after super().__init__() and before the dot check:
    if not name:
        raise ValueError("'name' may not be empty.")
That is exactly the requested behavior: Blueprint("", __name__) raises ValueError, and non-empty names still reach the existing dot-check error. I have no complaint about the implementation and I do not want you to change it.

BLOCKER (environment, not your patch): I could not obtain same-version public test execution. Three run_tests attempts on this exact v2 — (a) pytest targets ["tests/test_blueprints.py"], (b) same target plus a -k filter, (c) kind=full — all aborted during pytest STARTUP before collection. All three reported the same traceback tail:
  pytest.PytestAssertRewriteWarning: Module already imported so cannot be rewritten: pws_public_test_evidence_v141
raised from _pytest/config/__init__.py consider_env -> _import_plugin_specs (i.e. PYTEST_PLUGINS) -> assertion/rewrite.py mark_rewrite/_warn_already_imported.
Every run returned collected=null, tests_run=null, passed=null, and test_evidence.error "missing framework start or complete finish report". So zero tests actually executed; this is not a failing assertion and not caused by patch-1.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU (you are the designated delivery member): run your own run_tests on your final version. If you hit the same plugin-startup failure, it is environmental — do not rework the fix, just proceed to submit_integration with patch-1's content (and note the harness limitation). Your tree is the graded endpoint, so the final same-version test run and submission have to come from you. If you want, adding a small regression test asserting ValueError for an empty Blueprint name in tests/test_blueprints.py is welcome but optional.

I will re-review immediately: once a run actually executes tests on the exact final version and you have a fixed candidate, publish/hand it off and I will accept. If you publish any new patch, tell me the patch_id so I adopt that exact version rather than patch-1.

Rework published: patch-2 (base v1 -> v3, files_sha256 df18d478ce0b6b82c51cb512b468145e3e1885fc03b5360ab3d03377e49a1067). Please adopt, run public tests on this exact version and accept or request changes.

Content vs patch-1 (which you already verified as correct):
1. src/flask/blueprints.py — unchanged: `if not name: raise ValueError("'name' may not be empty.")` after super().__init__() and before the dot check.
2. tests/test_blueprints.py — NEW regression test test_empty_name_not_allowed: `with pytest.raises(ValueError): flask.Blueprint("", __name__)`, mirroring the existing test_dotted_name_not_allowed style. This is the optional regression test you suggested.

Same-version test evidence (honest): run_tests on this exact v3 (report test-report-1bf171c85706817d91538afb, targets tests/test_blueprints.py) again aborted during pytest startup, before collection. Exact stack: _pytest/config/__init__.py _preparse -> pluginmanager.consider_env -> _import_plugin_specs(os.environ["PYTEST_PLUGINS"]) while importing pws_public_test_evidence_v141, raising PytestAssertRewriteWarning "Module already imported so cannot be rewritten: pws_public_test_evidence_v141". Report shows collected=null, tests_run=null, evidence error "missing framework start or complete finish report", zero sessions. So no test executed on v3; I am not claiming a pass.

This reproduces your observation exactly, on a different version and a different selection, which further indicates a harness/plugin-startup defect rather than anything about this diff. Nothing in the diff can affect PYTEST_PLUGINS loading, and the new test only uses the existing `app`/`client` fixtures and flask.Blueprint.

Behavioral argument, independent of the harness: Blueprint.__init__ runs super().__init__(import_name, ...) then the added `if not name` guard, so Blueprint("", __name__) raises ValueError("'name' may not be empty."); Blueprint("app.ui", __name__) still hits the later dot check and raises its own ValueError; ordinary non-empty names still construct fine (unchanged path). The dot check can no longer be reached with an empty name, which is the requested behavior.

Suggested: adopt patch-2, run_tests on your exact adopted version if you want one more data point, then record your decision per policy (accept if you judge the candidate correct, noting the environmental startup failure). I will then submit_integration.

patch-2 (v3) adopted cleanly into my tree — no conflicts, files_sha256 df18d478ce0b6b82c51cb512b468145e3e1885fc03b5360ab3d03377e49a1067. I read the final diff myself.

VERDICT ON CODE: approved. src/flask/blueprints.py has, right after super().__init__() and before the dot check:
    if not name: raise ValueError("'name' may not be empty.")
    if "." in name: raise ValueError("'name' may not contain a dot '.' character.")
So Blueprint("", __name__) raises ValueError, non-empty dotted names still raise the dot error, and valid names reach self.name = name. tests/test_blueprints.py gains test_empty_name_not_allowed with pytest.raises(ValueError) around flask.Blueprint("", __name__), mirroring the existing dotted-name test. Nothing to change.

TEST EVIDENCE ON V3 — still zero tests executed, again environmental:
1) pytest targets ["tests/test_blueprints.py"] -> report test-report-ca43d8101ff2970a3b1dfab2, passed:false
2) kind=full -> report test-report-72faec859be0ebaa12369270, passed:false
Both have counts {collected:null, passed:null, failed:null, errors:null, tests_run:null} and test_evidence.error "missing framework start or complete finish report", with sessions [] and report_count 0. The traceback both times ends in pytest's own startup, before any collection:
  _pytest/config/__init__.py:1238 in _preparse -> self.pluginmanager.consider_env()
  :736 in consider_env -> self._import_plugin_specs(os.environ.get("PYTEST_PLUGINS"))

The name being rewritten is the evidence plugin itself, which is imported before pytest's own config parse. That is why it dies regardless of target, and why it is identical on v2 and v3. I also grepped tests/test_blueprints.py for that plugin name: no matches — nothing in the test file triggers it.
